headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace pair: Khoj can read indexed notes while Airflow can egress broadly, creating default-path leakage and downstream misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but Khoj reads indexed documents and can use RAG/web search, while Airflow can emit outputs that a user may manually feed into Khoj. That makes prompt injection possible only through unusual copy/paste or file bridging, with limited blast radius compared with default shared channels.
conditions: IF the operator copies Airflow-generated text into Khoj chat or indexed notes
IF a shared file or note is manually imported into both systems
mitigations: Keep Airflow outputs out of Khoj-indexed folders
Use a separate scratch workspace for Airflow artifacts
Strip instructions from copied text before pasting
Mark imported notes as data-only, not chat context
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files by default and can send queries to cloud or self-hosted servers; Airflow has broad network egress. If Airflow-generated artifacts contain sensitive notes and are indexed by Khoj, data can flow from the shared workspace into a networked backend. The pair therefore has a default-path leakage risk, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Airflow writes sensitive artifacts into a folder that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj is configured to use a cloud provider or external search provider
mitigations: Exclude sensitive Airflow output directories from Khoj indexing
Store secrets in a non-indexed vault path
Use self-hosted Khoj only
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is not runnable here and has no filesystem write capability listed, while Khoj can read files but cannot write or modify git state. Their mutable-resource overlap is therefore limited; the main conflict is read-side contention over shared documents, not destructive concurrent writes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same rapidly changing document set
IF an external orchestrator gives Airflow write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Separate read and write workspaces
Freeze shared inputs during runs
Use per-agent output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same notes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can treat indexed content as context, so Airflow-produced facts or summaries may be reused without verification if manually imported. Airflow can generate downstream artifacts, and Khoj can surface them authoritatively to the user, creating a plausible cascade from one agent's output into the other's responses.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are copied into Khoj notes or chat context
IF the operator relies on Khoj answers without checking the original Airflow source
mitigations: Require source links in imported summaries
Keep raw Airflow outputs separate from synthesized notes
Add a human verification step before reuse
Tag generated content as untrusted
requires-engineering: implement citation-preserving ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or configured search providers, while Airflow has broad network egress. If EU personal data or regulated notes are indexed and then processed by a non-local Khoj deployment, residency or retention obligations can be breached. Airflow is not itself the compliance driver here, so only Khoj is directly cited.
conditions: IF indexed documents contain EU personal data or regulated records
IF Khoj is deployed against a cloud provider or external search backend without a DPA
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to non-regulated notes
Use a self-hosted deployment with local storage
Purge sensitive documents from the index
Review retention settings before ingestion
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and deletion controls
